summary:
Lane: Blaster as trusted code, at the pinned fork 25c0ee0 (beta 46c8479 plus the one-line 6526c4b and its test). I read the tactic → Translate.main → Smt/Env process code, the optimizer's rule families and caches, the SMT translation (types, qualifiers, recursive functions, lambdas, matches, strings), and the fork diff. I tested the solver protocol, the string-literal escaping and the timeout behaviour directly on the installed Z3 5.3.1. I also searched upstream issues and PRs (GET only).

Verdict on the mechanics: sound. A goal closes only when the optimizer returns literally `True`, or when a fresh Z3 process prints exactly `unsat`. Timeouts, crashes, a missing or wrong z3, and unreadable output all end in an error or an open goal. No exception is turned into a result. All 310 blaster theorems use plain `blaster` with only `(timeout: 540|1200)` and `(verbose: 1)`. Fix 1 is correct and complete (it matches upstream main). The pre-fix bug could only give errors, or field-sort swaps that the qualifiers neutralize, never a false Valid for our goals. The README's #389 argument holds for every string operation that can reach the solver.

The real exposure is Blaster's own soundness at the pin, which the docs don't describe. (1) Its SMT encoding asserts lambda definitions without domain guards while extensionality is guarded. That is upstream #194: demonstrated `False`, still open, fix #268 unmerged, and its mechanism is present in our code. The same unguarded shape sits at recursive-function equations over `Nat`, which no upstream issue covers. Nobody has measured whether any of our 310 queries contains either construct. (2) The optimizer, not just Z3, is trusted: it writes `.prop`, which every statement is about, and it can close goals with no solver run. Upstream fixed three false-Valid optimizer bugs in exactly these code paths in the month before our pin. (3) Other open upstream soundness bugs present at the pin (#413, #225, #196, #195, #226, #368, #43) are not recorded in the docs. I assessed each as unreachable for these goals.

I wrote a diagnostic that builds no proofs. It re-runs Blaster on each theorem in only-smt-lib mode, lists the risky constructs, and replays each query: the full query, the background alone (to catch a vacuous ✅), the background plus the premises, and the query on Z3 4.15.2. That turns 'unmeasured' into a per-theorem answer.
checked_ok: Tactic closure: blasterTacticImp (Tactic.lean:54-64) admits only on `.Valid`. `.Falsified` throws, and `.Undetermined` replaces the goal and leaves it open, so the build errors. blasterAdmit (l.35-40) is the only use of blasterProven, and no proof module names blasterProven, sorry, admit or native_decide (grep).

Where Valid comes from: only `toResult optExpr = True` (Translate.lean:57; Env.lean:25-29), or getSatResult reading exactly `unsat\n` (Env.lean:538-542). `sat` → Falsified, `unknown` → Undetermined, and anything else (including EOF after a Z3 crash) → throwEnvError.

Solver protocol: each call starts a fresh z3 (`-in -smt2`) and issues one check-sat. Every setup and declaration command is checked for `success` (Env.lean:213-222). On Z3 5.3.1, `(set-option :print-success true)` echoes success and `(set-simplifier recfun-finder)` prints nothing, so the unchecked setSimplifier keeps the stream aligned; an unknown simplifier prints an error line that the next checked command rejects. Off-by-one or garbage output can only give an error, never an `unsat` read for the wrong query.

Timeouts: under Blaster's options (auto_config false, …), a `(set-option :timeout 1000)` query answered `unknown` after ~1 s (scratch z3/timeout2.smt2). That maps to Undetermined, so the goal stays open and the build errors. A missing z3 is an IO error, and a z3 lacking recfun-finder errors at setup.
Exceptions: the only `catch` in Blaster is instance synthesis (SynthInstance.lean:51), which maps a failure to 'no instance' (fewer rewrites). No exception is ever turned into a result.

Options: of 319 theorems, 310 use `blaster` with only `(timeout: 540)` (177), `(timeout: 1200)` (7), `(timeout: 540) (verbose: 1)` (7) or no option (119). The other 9 are `rfl` / `unfold … cases … <;> rfl`, which the kernel checks. only-smt-lib/only-optimize would only yield Undetermined, and solve-result/gen-cex only change logging in the tactic.
Local axioms: findLocalAxioms (Expr.lean:860-874) adds only Prop axioms declared in the current module, and the proof modules declare none (grep found no axiom/opaque/unsafe/extern/set_option).

Opaque constants: they are never unfolded. getFunBodyAux? unfolds only defnInfo, by value or by equation lemma (Rewriting/Utils.lean:579-603). opaqueInfo/axiomInfo become uninterpreted SMT functions whose codomain qualifiers come from their Lean types, which the real implementations satisfy. Partial defs (opaqueInfo) are handled the same way.

Recursion has no cut-off to truncate. unfold-depth is read nowhere. A recursive call is unfolded only when every explicit argument is a constructor (allExplicitParamsAreCtor), which terminates because the Lean function terminates. Otherwise the call is kept and translated with its full defining equation; that is sound apart from the unguarded-quantifier issue in the findings.

Arithmetic encodings (Env.lean:379-478) match Lean, zero divisors included: Nat.sub, Int ediv/emod/tdiv/tmod/fdiv/fmod, toNat, pow. The optimizer's Int/Nat rules also hold case by case: n/0, n%0, truncated subtraction chains, (n/N1)/N2, gcd normalization, cancellation, negSucc (OptimizeInt.lean, OptimizeNat.lean, OptimizeEq.lean arith rules).

Bool/Prop/ite/relational rules (OptimizeEq, OptimizeRelational including `≤ ⇒ ¬>` for Nat/Int/Bool/String, PropBinary, BoolPropBinary, PropNot, BoolNot, DecideBoolBinary, iteSimp?): I found no rule that is wrong for our types. The Lean theorems ite_equiv, dite_equiv and decide'_equiv prove the decide'/dite' replacements (Decidable.lean). BEq becomes `=` only when a LawfulBEq instance is synthesized (SynthInstance.lean:143-147).

#389 argument: the only string operations that reach SMT are str.++, str.len, str.< and =, plus literals. On Z3 5.3.1, the escapes \u{5c}u{41} (len 6), \u{ed} (237), doubled quote, \u{0} and \u{2ffff} all decode as Blaster assumes, and `str.<` on one-byte strings equals code-point order (difference unsat). Char-level operations can't be translated: no String selector exists, and Char's BitVec is rejected. So they error, never Valid. Opaque outputs are unconstrained SMT strings, which covers the real functions. The README's 'covers every bytestring' holds.

Fix 1 (6526c4b) is correct and complete. It is identical to upstream main a16614e (Quantifier.lean:946). Line 948 (`hashcons recRule.rhs`) is safe: each rule's right-hand side mentions its own inductive and constructors (the motive's binder type), so it shares only with that inductive's own terms. Before the fix, permuted names either failed Z3's sort check or coincided in SMT sort, and the qualifiers are built from Lean's field types (generatePredicateAssertions), so there was no false Valid for monomorphic instantiations. The fork's diff from beta is that one line plus its test (`git diff 46c8479 25c0ee0`).

Pins: the Blaster checkout is clean at 25c0ee0. 46c8479 is upstream beta's head today (GitHub compare: identical), and main's 8 extra commits are CI and benchmark only, so no upstream soundness fix is missing from our base.
Z3 binary: official 5.3.1, verified through GitHub. Blaster emits no SMT arrays or lambdas, so Z3 5.3.2's array and lambda soundness fixes don't apply.

Hash-consing ignores binder infos as well as names (Expr.lean sharedEq). The remaining reads (getFunEnvInfo → getImplicitParameters) can misclassify a parameter. A data parameter misread as implicit is folded into a specialized function instance (getInstApp/specializeLambda), not dropped. An implicit parameter misread as explicit gives arity or sort errors. I found no false-Valid path.
Upstream fixes for #287 (37e7b9b), #348 (03da4e1), negSucc (9fe7dc2), int div folding (#165) and funext (#98) are all in the pin, and their code is as described.
open_questions: Do any of the 310 SMT queries contain lambda definitions or Nat-parameter recursive functions, or a background that is unsat on its own? run-diag.sh (quick → modules → all) answers this per theorem.
Which ✅ were closed by the optimizer alone, with no Z3? The diag's OPT-ONLY rows list them.
Will the fork carry #268 (lambda/HOF guards), #414 (universe levels) and #223 (proof fields) once they merge upstream? Each changes the encoding or the optimizer, so everything would need a re-run.

The optimizer's disequality decisions (structEq?, isPatternMatch) assume maximal sharing, i.e. equal literals and constants are the same pointer. Every entry point I read hash-conses (toPropExpr, getFunBody, inferTypeEnv, the instantiate/beta helpers), but I did not check every expression builder.

summary: I audited the PlutusCoreBlaster fork at the pinned 68c5399 as the model of Cardano's script machine. It sits clean at SV/.lake/packages/PlutusCore and differs from upstream 1c23de8 in exactly five non-test files. I read every non-test change line by line (the Fq1-as-Nat change, the opaque aliases for ByteStringToInteger, XorByteString and SerializeData, and the BLS12-381 operand-order fix), plus the CEK step function, the builtin dispatch, the flat decoder and the term reflection, and PlutusCoreBlaster's conformance generator and runner. I also checked its last conformance run on GitHub (logs read only). I decoded all 13 scripts the proofs load with aiken 1.1.24: the three Seedelf scripts, the five classic Lovejoin scripts, the four templates and the v2 applied mix_logic. Verdict: for every construct and builtin these scripts use, the model matches Plutus V3 (post-Conway, variant E), and I found nothing that makes a ✅ false. Each alias's body is exactly the original call, with the same arity and argument order, and its uninterpreted result can only add interpretations. The operand-order fix is complete: every other multi-argument binding in every builtin file is already in source order. All crypto builtins the scripts use are Lean `opaque`, and Blaster never unfolds them. Every validator's only halting value is `(con unit ())`. Every `case` is the `case (constr 0 …) f` idiom. Steps' stepsUsed runs the same machine with the same argument application and step semantics as cekExecuteProgram. Three gaps remain. (1) Every proof loads its script through the flat decoder, and the conformance suite never runs that decoder; the circumstantial evidence that it is right is strong, and FlatVsText.lean settles it. (2) `isSuccessful` accepts a halt with any value, and nothing checks that a module applies its script to the right number of arguments. Today all 227 are right, but a slip would make whole families of ✅s vacuous without any failing signal. (3) Conformance has never been run on the pinned commit, and README names an older pin with three changes where the build uses five.
checked_ok: Pin integrity: SV/.lake/packages/PlutusCore is at 68c5399 with a clean tree, and its non-test diff from 1c23de8 is exactly Basic.lean (Fq1), G1.lean (ToExpr), Bitwise.lean (two aliases), Data.lean (one alias) and Crypto.lean (operand order).

ByteStringToInteger alias: the body `(PLC.byteStringToInteger e s).toNat` loses nothing, because PLC.byteStringToInteger always returns `.ofNat _` (Bitwise/Basic.lean:89-91). The dispatch `[bs, e] => .ofNat (alias e bs.data)` (Bitwise.lean:58) gives the original value, and the Nat result adds only the true fact n ≥ 0.

XorByteString alias: the body is literally `PLC.xorByteString e b c` (Bitwise.lean:83), and the dispatch `[op2, op1, e] => alias e op1.data op2.data` (:89) is the same call as before; `false` means truncate and `true` means pad with zeros, as in Plutus.

SerializeData alias: the body is `PLC.encodeData d` and the dispatch is otherwise unchanged (Data.lean:168, :173); returning an `Option` only adds failing interpretations, which keeps every Valid sound.

Fq1.t as a Nat: the constructor is private and every value is built by Fq1.ofNat (mod p); ToExpr reflects through ofNat, and add/sub/neg/mul/inv, compress and ofBytesWithCheck compute the same canonical values as before. Conformance (1.64.0.0) passed on #72's head with every BLS case, and a larger symbolic Point type only strengthens ∀-goals.

CEK argument order: each argument is consed onto the list (CekMachine.lean:92, 94, 102, 104), so a builtin sees its arguments last-first; the integer builtins bind `[op2, op1] => f op1 op2`, which conformance checks on non-commutative cases (subtract, lessThan, divide, mod).

Operand-order fix complete: the six BLS bindings now read `[y, x] => f x y` (Crypto.lean:119, 131, 147, 159, 211, 215). Every other multi-argument binding in every builtin file is already in source order: G1/G2 scalarMul, hashToGroup, millerLoop, multiScalarMul, the three signature verifiers, integerToByteString, byteStringToInteger, and/or/xor, append, cons, slice, index, chooseData, constrData, mkPairData, mkCons, dropList, ifThenElse, chooseUnit, trace, expModInteger, shift/rotate/readBit/writeBits/replicateByte, appendString.

Builtins the scripts use (aiken decode of all 13): 42 in total, and no G2, millerLoop, mulMlResult, finalVerify or hashToGroup. The only multi-argument opaque ones are G1 add, equal and scalarMul, byteStringToInteger and xorByteString; all are bound in source order, and each is symmetric or distinguished by argument type on real values, so a spec written in the model's order keeps its real meaning.

Opaque builtins and Blaster: these are Lean `opaque` with a body (no @[irreducible], implemented_by or extern): the 6 hashes, the 3 signature verifiers, every G1/G2/pairing operation, expModInteger and the 3 fork aliases. multiScalarMul is a transparent fold over the opaque add and scalarMul, and no script uses it. Blaster's optimizer never unfolds opaqueInfo (getFunBodyAux? handles only defnInfo; isNotFoldable calls isAxiomOrOpaque). Every crypto builtin the scripts use is opaque.

Flat decoder spot checks: term tags 0–9, type tags 0–8, zigzag integers, byte-aligned bytestring chunks, and the version gate on constr/case (≥1.1.0, tag < 2^64) match the spec. The builtin table matches aiken's encoder for all 91 active entries, and aiken decode→encode round-trips all 13 scripts byte-exactly.

Conformance setup: with --exclude-not-implemented, only array and value builtins are skipped (notImplementedPaths); evaluation-failure and parse-error cases are guarded `true`. In plutus master every test directory has exactly one .uplc file and no subdirectories, so the walker drops nothing. #72's 1.64.0.0 run built every builtin these scripts use (serialiseData has no cases to build), plus term/case (11), term/constr (11) and constant-case (32).

Semantics spot checks: divide/mod are Int.fdiv/Int.fmod, flooring (conformance's modInteger(-503, 1777777777) = 1777777274); quotient/remainder are tdiv/tmod; the default variant is E (Default/Basic.lean:54-55), under which consByteString errors outside [0,255] (conformance cases 256 and -88 fail as expected); unConstrData, unIData, unBData, unListData, unMapData, headList and tailList error on the wrong shape or an empty list; integerToByteString checks w<0, w>8192, w=0 ∧ log2 n ≥ 65536, n<0 and n not fitting in w bytes; byteStringToInteger maps empty to 0 and reads little-endian as the reversed bytes; lengthOfByteString counts characters; ifThenElse and chooseList receive evaluated values, i.e. are strict.
The specs' Int.fmod is literally the model's modInteger (BuiltinFunctions/Integer.lean:69) and, for q > 0, Haskell's floor `mod`; v2's mix_logic does call modInteger(byteStringToInteger True x, q).

Unit result: all 13 validators end in `force (ifThenElse COND (delay (con unit ())) (delay error))`, written plainly or as `case (constr 0 …) ifThenElse`, with the ifThenElse binding confirmed among the top-level lets. A COND that isn't a Bool errors, so every halt is a unit, and no 'spec ⇒ isSuccessful' ✅ counts a non-unit result.

All 660 `case` nodes in the 10 Lovejoin scripts are `case (constr 0 …) f` with one branch, and every script is UPLC 1.1.0, so the model's case-on-builtin-constants arms are never exercised. Neither is its lack of PLC 1.2.0 case-on-Data, which plutus master tests; the 1.64.0.0 suite it passed has no such cases.

Applied scripts equal their templates: v2's applied mix_logic is structurally `[[Template mix_logic P] N]` (de Bruijn comparison) and the classic mix_box is `[Template mix_box L]`, so applying the parameters at run time in the model gives the same term. Separately, all 227 `#prep_uplc` argument functions apply exactly the script's arity.

stepsUsed/stepsWith vs cekExecuteProgram: both use the same `step default` (variant E) from the same `initialState (applyParams body args)`. A reported count N is the number of steps to Halt or Error, and runStepsPreservingState returns that state for any limit ≥ N, because its Halt/Error arm comes before the 0 arm. stepsUsed needs fuel N+1 to report it: an off-by-one, but only in the safe direction.

No hidden assumptions: cekExecuteProgram doesn't use the sorry'd runStepsWithBudget; the sorry'd *Lemmas modules are outside PlutusCore.UPLC's import closure; PlutusCore, Cryptograph and CardanoLedgerApi declare no axioms.

mkCons deviation: the model doesn't check a generic ConstList's element type, while Plutus does. That only makes the model more permissive. Data and pair-of-data lists are typed (conformance's mkCons-fail passes), and Aiken never emits a mismatched mkCons, so no ✅ is affected.

Concrete fidelity: Steps' KAT runs halt with their honest proofs (Seedelf Register valid after 1281 steps, v2 Mix KAT after 11497, owner KATs after 3099/3195), and the classic and v2 owner proofs are bound to the context hash through serialise_data. So the Lean bodies of blake2b, the G1 operations, byteStringToInteger, integerToByteString and the CBOR encoder agree with the real implementations on these inputs. The xor body is exercised by the v2 Mix KAT.

Has the fork's own `make check_tests` been run at 68c5399 itself? The local traces (BuiltinOperandOrder, SymbolicPoints, ByteStringToIntegerSymbolic: Valid or Expected Falsified) don't record which commit they were built at, and the xor alias has no test of its own.

summary: Provenance audit: are the verified bytes the right bytes, and are they applied the right way? I checked all 13 .hex files the Lean imports. I recomputed their hashes, decoded them fully against seedelf-core's pins and on-chain reference outputs, and replayed the three extract scripts in scratch. I rebuilt every source tree in my scratch dir with network off: Seedelf 5b82530 with Aiken v1.1.9, Lovejoin classic c1239fb, the 8131b1d templates and v2 5cc3631, the last three with v1.1.24. I checked the cached stdlib v4.0.0 file by file against GitHub's v4.0.0 tag tree (66/66 match). I re-applied every template parameter with aiken blueprint apply. I traced how the Lean side applies parameters (toTerm, applyParams, all 231 #prep_uplc argument lists) and checked the pins against the manifest, the package HEADs and all 159 build traces. Verdict: the bytes are right. Every hash matches the docs and seedelf-core. The Seedelf and classic hex files are byte-identical to the script_refs of the on-chain reference outputs seedelf-core holds. All four source trees rebuild to exactly the imported bytes. Each applied script is literally its template wrapped in Data-constant applications, in the order on-chain hashes pin, and the Lean modules pass the same Data terms in the same order before the ScriptContext. The problems are in the evidence chain, not the bytes. (1) high: Lake does not treat the .hex files as build inputs. After a re-extract, check.sh would replay old ✅s over bytes no longer on disk. (2) medium: in this tree, the six Seedelf proof modules (28 ✅, WalletRegister among them) were last built on an earlier PlutusCoreBlaster pin and before Wallet.lean's scalarOf change. The README still names c7d8741. (3) medium: nothing outside seedelf-verification pins v2's verified template 7fb45b75 yet, so 'the template theorems already hold for' the v2 launch has no enforced tie to the bytes that will be launched. Two low proposals add an independent decoder cross-check (a Lean module for the owner) and a reference-output check in extract.sh. Disclosure: I once ran `~/.elan/toolchains/leanprover--lean4---v4.24.0/bin/lean --version` to read its commit. It is a version query only, no build or elaboration, but it breaks the never-run-lean rule.
checked_ok: CBOR framing: all 13 imported .hex files are exactly one CBOR bytestring (0x58 for always_false 63 B and reference_holder 94 B, 0x59 for the rest), with no trailing bytes and no whitespace. The payload is a flat 1.1.0 program, not a second CBOR layer, which is the ledger's PlutusBinary.

Hashes: blake2b-224(0x03‖bytes) of each hex gives exactly the documented hashes: wallet 94bca9c0, seedelf 84967d91, always_false 6777ba4d, mix_box c145c10f, mix_logic 0dad3046, fee_contract a072c7e8, one_shot_mint f5592689, reference_holder 288fea77, v2 template 7fb45b75, v2 test launch 60294352, templates mix_box 2365a62d, one_shot_mint 6878ed6f, fee_contract 3698bbfd.

Seedelf pins: the hashes equal constants.rs variant 1 (94bca9c0, 84967d91; sizes 629/519). Full CBOR decode shows wallet.hex and seedelf.hex byte-identical to the script_ref of MAINNET_/PREPROD_WALLET and _SEEDELF in references.rs. Those outputs sit at always_false's address 716777ba4d…

Classic pool pins: the hashes equal Protocol::of mainnet (c145c10f, 0dad3046, id f5592689, fee a072c7e8) and REFERENCE_HOLDER_HASH. mix_box.hex and mix_logic.hex are byte-identical to LOVEJOIN_MAINNET_MIX_BOX/MIX_LOGIC script_refs. The mainnet reference UTxO's datum names c145c10f/0dad3046/a072c7e8 and holds f5592689.lovejoin at 288fea77. c1239fb's addresses.json agrees and records aiken v1.1.24+bacbeb3. c1239fb is the only commit touching artifacts/mainnet.

Templates vs seedelf-core: Template/Scripts/{one_shot_mint,mix_box,fee_contract}.hex and Lovejoin/Scripts/reference_holder.hex are byte-identical to templates.rs's bundled 8131b1d constants, with hashes equal to templates_are_frozen. Only mix_logic differs (v2 7fb45b75 vs 8131b1d's 62befd1e), as documented.

Extract scripts reproduce the committed files: I replayed extract.sh and extract-lovejoin.sh in scratch from git show 5b82530/c1239fb. Every .hex, concrete/build/*.flat and .plutus came out byte-identical. extract-lovejoin-v2.sh's five outputs equal my independent build. Each script's hash constants agree with seedelf-core, the docs and on-chain pool data (dc6abe3b and 20aae476 from lovejoin-pools.json's 5 ₳ pool).

v2 reproducibility: git archive 5cc3631 plus aiken v1.1.24+bacbeb3 (offline via unshare -rn; stdlib v4.0.0 cache matches GitHub tag v4.0.0's tree blob for blob, 66/66) gives compiledCode equal to all four Template hex files and reference_holder.hex. A scratch build of 8131b1d reproduces templates.rs byte for byte, mix_logic 62befd1e included.

v2 diff: git -C LJ2 diff 8131b1d 5cc3631 touches one file, contracts/lib/lovejoin/sigma_or.ak (+35/−10). xor32 gains `expect bytearray.length(left) == 32` and `expect bytearray.length(right) == 32`, its doc comment is rewritten, and 8 boundary tests are appended. 5cc3631's only parent is 8131b1d = templates.rs COMMIT. The compiled v2 mix_logic has 2 more lengthOfByteString calls than 8131b1d's.

Source to bytes, Seedelf: 5b82530's seedelf-contracts built with Aiken v1.1.9+2217206 (--trace-level silent) and the acabcafe seed applied reproduces wallet, seedelf and always_false byte for byte. So specs written against `git show 5b82530:…` are written against the right source.

Source to bytes, classic pool: c1239fb's contracts built with v1.1.24 and applied to the bootstrap parameters (seed ba815aa5…#2, 288fea77; then f5592689, 'lovejoin'; then L 0dad3046) reproduce the classic one_shot_mint, mix_logic, mix_box and fee_contract byte for byte.

Parameter application (tooling): aiken blueprint apply on my build at (B abab×28, B 'lovejoin') reproduces V2/Scripts/mix_logic.hex byte for byte. The swapped order gives 13313bc7…, so on-chain hashes pin the order. The decoded applied program is literally [[T (con data (B #abab…))] (con data (B #6c6f76656a6f696e))], and the classic mix_box is literally [T_mixbox (con data (B #0dad3046…))]. Nothing is optimized after application. seedelf-core's apply() (Program::apply_data in order) and Lovejoin's 00-build-reference.sh (blueprint apply, CBOR atoms in order) agree.

Parameter application (Lean): toTerm x = Term.Const (Const.Data (toData x)), with ByteString→Data.B and Integer→Data.I, the same Data constants blueprint apply uses. applyParams folds left, so the first param is innermost, then the ScriptContext. Scanned all 231 #prep_uplc: 98 mixLogicTemplate pass [P, nftName, ctx]; 28 mixBoxTemplate [L, ctx]; 5 oneShotMintTemplate [s, i, rh, ctx]; 5 feeContractTemplate [P, nftName, ctx]. The 16 mixLogicV2 modules and all classic and Seedelf ones pass only [ctx]. nftName = 'lovejoin' as a ByteString of byte-chars (no UTF-8) = 6c6f76656a6f696e. Template.Steps.stepsWith also applies params before ctx.

Decoding: the 8 concrete/build/*.flat files equal the hex payloads, and `aiken uplc decode` of each .flat is identical to the decode of its .hex. All 13 decode as program 1.1.0 with plausible sizes (61 B to 3484 B of flat). #import_uplc single_cbor_hex rejects trailing CBOR bytes. The decoder is unmodified upstream code, and its builtin tag table is correct for every builtin used.

Pins as built: lakefile revs = lake-manifest rev/inputRev = package HEADs (Blaster 25c0ee0, PlutusCore 68c5399, CardanoLedgerApi 9938562). The working trees are clean, with no assume-unchanged or skip-worktree. Blaster 25c0ee0 = 46c8479 + 6526c4b + the #454 test; PlutusCore 1c23de8..68c5399 is only fork commits. The package builds postdate their checkouts (the PlutusCore modules changed 96a36cb→68c5399 were rebuilt after 08:59:39). All 159 traces use the SV/.lake/packages LEAN_PATH and lean v4.24.0 (commit 797c613 = the GitHub tag v4.24.0). Lean-blaster 25c0ee0 and CardanoLedgerApi 9938562 exist on GitHub; 68c5399 is local-only, which chunk 42 documents as a publishing step.

Current Lovejoin ✅s are on current bytes: every Lovejoin module trace carries the current libPlutusCore.so hash. Each Scripts olean was built after its hex content's only commit, and the tree is clean, so no recorded Lovejoin ✅ is over stale bytes.

extract-lovejoin-v2.sh's cleanliness check (`git diff --quiet HEAD -- contracts`) ignores untracked files and the gitignored contracts/build/packages. The four templates_are_frozen hashes and my independent git-archive build with a GitHub-verified stdlib cover that gap, so the committed v2 bytes are sound.

summary: I read all 11 modules in SV/Seedelf/ against 5b82530's wallet.ak, schnorr.ak, seedelf.ak, token_name.ak, logic.ak and always_false.ak. I also decoded all three deployed scripts with `aiken uplc decode`, traced PlutusCoreBlaster's wiring for every builtin the spec calls, checked CardanoLedgerApi's V3 encodings and the build traces, and ran Aiken's evaluator on honest contexts (the repo's own vectors). Verdict on the wallet: the core spec is faithful. `schnorrAccepts` matches `prove` and the bytes line by line: blake2b_224 over ((g‖g_r)‖u)‖vkh, z and c decoded big-endian with 0 ≤ n < q (q is BLS12-381's r), the three uncompress calls, and equal(g^z, add(g_r, u^c)) in the script's operand order. No check is missing on either side. The checked equation with that Fiat–Shamir input is strong Fiat–Shamir Schnorr bound to vkh, and with list.has over extra_signatories it gives the replay protection CLAUDE.md describes. The iff means what it should in its scenario: every path ends within 1306 steps, and the only value the script can halt with is unit. The wallet reads only signatories (txInfo field 8), so the property carries to real transactions, by reading the bytes rather than by proof. The 18 NoLock shapes partition every non-Register datum. The policy side is weaker than claimed. PolicyAmount's context uses a token name that `generate` never gives for its input, so every mint fails on the name, and the ✅ says nothing about the mint's `1 == amt` (high). PolicyForeign's mint theorem is vacuous the same way (low; the state can't occur on chain). PolicyBurn's two counted ✅ can't be recorded at all, because the module always fails (medium). Every Seedelf trace in this tree, WalletRegister's included, predates the current pin and the current scalarOf (medium; build-evidence's lane). Lean modules for the owner to run are in /tmp/claude-1000/-home-logic-Documents-LogicalMechanism-Seedelf-Wallet/bb70aec6-fc56-4ac3-ac4c-9981682502da/scratchpad/seedelf-spec/lean/.
checked_ok: schnorrAccepts against 5b82530's schnorr.ak prove and the decoded wallet UPLC (scratch wallet.pp.txt:72-101): c = blake2b_224(appendByteString(appendByteString(appendByteString(g, g_r), u), vkh)), the same order as fiat_shamir_heuristic(generator, g_r_b, public_value, bound) and seedelf-crypto's create_proof; one decode helper for z and c, byteStringToInteger(True, ·) with lessThanEqualsInteger(0, n) && lessThanInteger(n, q), and q = 0x73eda753…00000001, checked equal in Python; uncompress of g, u and g_r; equal(scalarMul(z, G), add(uncompress(g_r), scalarMul(c, U))), in the order the spec states.

The model's builtins call exactly what the spec calls: appendByteString [op2, op1] → op1 ++ op2; G1 add and equal [y, x] → f x y (the operand-order fix); scalarMul (integer, point); uncompress through Except.toOption, so .error is the Error state; ByteStringToInteger is `.ofNat (byteStringToIntegerOpaque e bs.data)`, the alias scalarOf calls; blake2b_224 is the opaque PLC.blake2b_224.

Nothing the Register branch checks is missing from the spec, and the spec adds nothing: two scalar decodes (expect Some), three uncompress calls, the equation, then list.has. The purpose, datum shape and redeemer shape checks come earlier and the scenario fixes them. The empty z_b decodes to 0, a valid scalar (no forgery: g_r = -c·u would need a hash fixed point); z_b has no length limit, which only allows leading-zero malleability, and the script integrity hash covers the redeemer anyway.

Σ-protocol: the hash covers the statement (g, u) and the commitment g_r (strong Fiat–Shamir), with a 224-bit challenge below q. The concatenation is unambiguous because uncompress requires 48 canonical bytes per point (opaque in the model), and vkh comes last. Binding vkh in c and requiring it in extra_signatories stops rollback replay, and stops moving a proof from one re-randomised register to another. Nothing soundness needs is absent from the script except non-identity points, which are left off-chain by design (CLAUDE.md).

wallet_register_spend_iff, direction by direction (facts 3 and 4): ⇒ covers every run of the scenario, since all paths end within 1306 steps (valid 1281, bad proof 1119, other signer 1306) against a limit of 2500, and halting with any value includes halting with unit. ⇐ gives ledger success because the only value the script can halt with is `con unit ()` (outer ifThenElse); the same holds for the policy and always_false, so fact 4's 'any value' gap is closed by the bytes.

Steps' stepsUsed runs the same machine as #prep_uplc's exec: initialState (applyParams body [toTerm ctx]) with `step default` (variant E), as cekExecuteProgram → runStepsPreservingState does. Only consByteString depends on the variant, and C and E agree on it.

The deployed wallet reads ScriptContext fields 1 and 2 and ScriptInfo index 1 with its datum (the outRef is bound but unused), and from TxInfo only field 8, only after prove succeeds. CardanoLedgerApi's encoding puts signatories at 8, mint at 4 and inputs at 0, ScriptInfo SpendingScript is Constr 1 [ref, Option], and Option is Constr 0 [d] / Constr 1 []. Fact 6 (the spent input missing from txInfoInputs) is irrelevant to this script.

WalletNoLock's partition: Data has exactly five constructors (Data/Basic.lean:19-24). The 18 families plus Some(Constr 0 [B, B]) are exhaustive and disjoint: None; B, I, List, Map; Constr k with k = n+1 and k = negSucc n; Constr 0 with 0, 1 and ≥3 fields; [non-B, any]; [B, non-B]. The UPLC's chooseData/chooseList cascade (wallet.pp.txt:35-120) returns True on exactly those and runs prove only on Constr 0 with exactly two B fields. The ledger gives None or Some(d), and a datum hash resolves to its datum or the transaction fails phase 1.

'Any well-formed proof': the redeemer is validated strictly before the datum is looked at, and must be exactly Constr 0 [B, B, B]. In concrete runs (evals/wallet_redeemers.sh), 2 or 4 fields, an I field, Constr 1 or I 0 crash even with no datum, while [B, B, B] with None or Some(I 7) returns unit. The theorems quantify over every z, g_r, vkh and signer, and the NoLock branches never read the TxInfo.

WalletPurpose: the purpose test (constr index 1) is the first thing after unpacking the context, so the five isUnsuccessful theorems, which cover all five non-spending V3 purposes with their payloads symbolic, hold for any transaction and redeemer by reading the bytes. AlwaysFalse's UPLC unpacks the context and errors unconditionally, so its isUnsuccessful theorem is general.

Strong forms: AlwaysFalse, WalletPurpose, PolicyAmount, PolicyForeign and PolicyBurn's counted theorems all use isUnsuccessful; WalletNoLock uses isSuccessful; each is self-checking against a step limit set too small. PolicyBurn's counted theorems fail for the right reason: in their context the burn block passes (pid, 5eed0e1f prefix, -1) and the mint block's consByteString(256 or -1) errors. The README counts only those two; burn_at_0, burn_at_255 and PolicyMint's two are the BitVec-parked ones listed under 'Not proved'.

Steps' valid Register spend is the theorem's scenario exactly: spendCtx (some (Constr 0 [B g1, B u0])) z0 gr0 vkh0 vkh0 = registerArgs g1 u0 z0 gr0 vkh0 vkh0. It halts after 1281 steps, and schnorrAccepts evaluates true through the builtins' compiled implementations, so the right-hand side is satisfiable under the real interpretation. Aiken's evaluator with blst agrees (concrete/wallet_register.sh, which I ran: unit, and every change crashes). 'Other signer' errors after 1306, which covers the second conjunct.

summary: I checked v2's Mix spec and how its iff is split into theorems. Sources: MixSpec, MixAnySpec, Mix3Spec, the five generated Specs and all 33 theorem modules, compared against LJ2 5cc3631 (validate_mix, walk_outputs, verify_pre, xor32, hash.ak, bls.ak, stdlib v4's scalar, bitwise and g1 modules) and against the decoded UPLC of Template/Scripts/mix_logic.hex. Verdict: nothing critical, high or medium. Each spec function follows the script line for line: the hash preimage and its order, both xor32 length checks, z's checks, `from_int` as `Int.fmod`, the G1 operand order, and the uncompress(compress(uncompress a')) form, which the UPLC confirms. On real BLS12-381 that form is exactly the intended relation. The Fiat–Shamir input binds n, the box in's (a, b), every box out's raw (a', b'), every commitment, and ctx. ctx covers the box outs' datums, the box value n times, and M. The script forces each box out to be determined by its datum plus the pool, and M identifies the pool, so no pool data an attacker controls is left out of the hash. Composition is complete for all eight families: KAT n = 2 and 3; ADA n = 2, 3, 4; token n = 2, 3, 4. An independent parser found every conjunct covered, each box over its own variables, no index slip, and each Passes assuming exactly the spec plus natural side conditions. That makes 82 general theorems and 20 on the test launch, each with a ✅ in its trace. Regenerating with gen-lovejoin-mix.py in a scratch copy gave a byte-identical V2/ (36 modules rewritten, `diff -r` empty). Chunk 42's MixChallenges lift argument is sound. The findings are low and info only: the iff is put together in prose over distinct constants (a Lean module that does it mechanically is provided); the iff's side conditions are missing from chunk 42 and the Box docs; "No value leaves the pool" overstates, because box-in values and the tail outputs are bound by nothing; the scenario's transaction shape is not a real Mix's; and the Mix3* traces predate a docs/verbose-only edit.

Every KAT proof block lists t0, t1, c, z in that order (the generator's length assertion couldn't tell c from z).

The spec follows the Aiken line for line. ctx = (('' ‖ d1) ‖ … ‖ dn) ‖ (('' ‖ v) ‖ … v) ‖ M, matching walk_outputs' accumulators and validate_mix:202-206. The header is domain ‖ 03 ‖ from_int_big_endian(n, 1) ‖ a ‖ b (hash.ak:93-113). with_branches folds over the statements in output order (list.reverse of the consed accumulator), with_commitments folds over the branches, c_global = blake2b_256(… ‖ ctx). The xor fold starts from the literal zero32, and xor32 checks both operands with the right one being c_j (sigma_or.ak:77-81, 166-172). z must be 32 bytes and below q; c is reduced mod q; from_int = State(n % field_prime) (stdlib v4 bitwise.ak:133-135); `%` is modInteger = Int.fmod (PCB Integer.lean:65-70); q equals 0x73eda7…01. g1.scale(p, k) is scalarMul(to_int k, p); the checks are equal(scale(z, a), add(t0, scale(c, a'))) and the same for b.

The decoded UPLC (aiken uplc decode --hex --cbor Template/Scripts/mix_logic.hex) confirms the spec's forms. walk_outputs stores `bData(compress(uncompress(unBData ap)))` and each branch uses `uncompress(unBData field 2/3)`. The box in's points are let-bound and used directly. The xor is `xorByteString False acc c` after `lengthOfByteString` checks on both. The branch fields are read t0 = 0, t1 = 1, c = 2, z = 3. The domain‖03 prefix is one constant. Halting means unit: the only `(con unit ())` sits under the final ifThenElse, so isSuccessful really is acceptance.

PCB dispatch matches the spec's aliases. xorByteString hands `xorByteStringOpaque e op1 op2` the first UPLC argument as op1 (Bitwise.lean:83-90), as the spec's `xor32 left right` does. byteStringToInteger returns `.ofNat (byteStringToIntegerOpaque e bs.data)` (Bitwise.lean:51-59), as the spec writes it.

The uncompress(compress(uncompress a')) form is sound. On real BLS12-381, uncompress returns only subgroup points from their canonical encoding, and compress gives that encoding back, so U(C(P)) = P for every P that U returns. The script's relation is therefore exactly the intended DH-tuple relation, accepting and refusing the same points.

Fiat–Shamir binding. Box outs are fully determined by datum plus pool: output_at_script forces Script(M) with no stake and no reference script, the value must equal box_value, and the datum must be inline (mix_logic.ak:275-278). M identifies the pool, since mix_box is parameterised by L and L by (P, 'lovejoin'), and the box value is in ctx too. n is in the header and n ≤ 255 is asserted. The preimage parses one way only: points are 48 bytes (decode and uncompress), ctx is 32, n is 1 byte. Owner (01) and Mix (03) use different statement ids. The redeemer is nothing but the proofs. Not bound: the box ins' out refs (settled same-datum case), the tail, other inputs, the fee.

MixChallenges. mix_refuses_a_challenge_not_32_bytes quantifies over c11, c12, c21 and c22 only. It fixes mixLogicV2 at the test launch, the KAT transaction (inputs, outputs, reference input, fee, withdrawal) and every KAT t0, t1 and z, under a 30000-step limit. It holds for every interpretation of xor, byteStringToInteger, the hash and BLS, so the failure must come from xor32's non-opaque length checks. Chunk 42's lift (line 39) is sound: in every family's spec, xor32 checks the right operand c_j and the nested matches pass none along. So any c_j whose length isn't 32 makes xorOfChallenges… none and challengeHolds… false, and that box's challenge theorem gives isUnsuccessful, for every pool (template families) and n = 2 to 4. The step is a definitional unfolding, not a Lean theorem.

Step limits are not a weakness here. In every family the needs theorems (Error within the limit) and Passes (Halt within the limit) between them cover every input that meets the side conditions, so no run in the scenario can exhaust. summary: I worked through v2's Mix and Owner scenarios: V2/Mix (the KAT context), MixAny, MixAny3/4, MixTok2/3/4, Mix3, the …Out, …OutSteps, …Outputs and …Datums families with gen-lovejoin-mix-outputs.py, MixOutputs, MixDatums, V2/Owner, and OwnAny1-4 with gen-lovejoin-owner.py. I checked them against the v2 source (LJ2 5cc3631) and against the bytes themselves. I decoded the template's UPLC (7fb45b75…) and pretty-printed walk_outputs and validate_mix. I also ran 60+ concrete transactions through Aiken's evaluator on the applied script (60294352…), using only honest proofs: Lovejoin's own KAT proofs, and Schnorr proofs built the way concrete/lovejoin_owner.sh builds them. Verdict: the ✅s in this area are true for what they state, and the fields they fix are ones the script never reads. The script reads only TxInfo fields 0-2 (inputs, reference inputs, outputs), its redeemer, and the ScriptInfo constructor. The withdrawal credential is bound and never used. The Owner code is identical line for line to the classic pool's. But the scenarios are narrower than the claims made for them in three security-relevant places, all undocumented: (1) a token pool's box out never has its token swapped or dropped; (2) a box out's inline datum is never anything but Constr 0 [B _, B _]; (3) no transaction ever has a well-formed box beyond the n that have proofs, and no redeemer ever has the wrong number of proofs or branches. Beyond that, no scenario has the shape of a real transaction: the wallet's Mix has a payer input and reference-script inputs, and the wallet's withdrawal has no payer and one output. In every case the bytes already do the right thing: the decoded UPLC shows the whole-value equalsData check, the strict cast's exact-two-fields check and the filter_map count, and the Aiken runs crash or halt as the source says. So these are gaps in the proofs, not flaws in v2. To close them I wrote 27 Lean modules: 97 Blaster theorems, 9 rfl lemmas and 45 concrete #eval runs. They cover the ADA pool at n=2, the token pool at n=2 and the template Owner. I couldn't compile them (no Lean runs allowed). They copy the existing modules' patterns, and I checked their brackets and all 97 .prop argument lists against their args functions. Each Steps module's expected lines match Aiken runs on the same contexts. They need the owner's run.

How the script reads them. Reference inputs: every one is walked with quantity_of(P, lovejoin) == 1, exactly one carrier is required, its datum must be inline and cast to the 8-field ReferenceDatum. Lake only replays a saved log when all of these match.

summary:
Encoding lane: whether the scenarios are real Plutus V3 script contexts. I checked every CardanoLedgerApiBlaster V3 IsData instance the scenarios use (the package is at 9938562 and unmodified) against plutus-ledger-api V3 and against Aiken stdlib v2.2.0 (Seedelf, 5b82530) and v4.0.0 (Lovejoin, c1239fb and 5cc3631). I read the stdlib sources from GitHub. I also checked every piece of hand-written Data against the Aiken types at the deployed commits. All of it is faithful: constructor indices, field orders, Maybe, Interval, treasury fields, V3 TxId as bare bytes, Credential-keyed withdrawals, TxCert, ScriptInfo and ScriptPurpose.

To run the same bytes as Lean without running Lean, I wrote a Python mirror of the IsData instances. With it I rebuilt every Steps.lean context and ran each one with Aiken v1.1.24 on the same deployed bytes. Every outcome matched Steps.lean's halt/error line: Seedelf 13/13, classic Lovejoin 17/17, v2 11/11, templates 7/7. The Lean-computed owner vectors also pass on the mirror's bytes, which confirms the serialisation at byte level.

The unrealistic fields change no verdict. Identical Aiken costs show the scripts never read them: the spent input missing from inputs, empty ids, the empty redeemers map, unsorted fee-scenario inputs, the `always` range.

The real problems are in what some scenarios contain, not in how they are encoded. No ✅ is false.
1. PolicyAmount's and PolicyForeign's token name isn't the one `generate` gives, so every mint in those scenarios fails no matter what. The mint half of "any amount other than ±1 fails" is unsupported. PolicyMint is blocked on BitVec, so no proven theorem constrains a Seedelf mint at all.
2. The token-pool "exact box value" families leave out the ledger's encodings of a box out with the token kept back, renamed or swapped, of an extra policy sorting before the pool's, and of a second name under the pool's policy. Their q = 0 case is a zero entry the ledger never produces.
3. PolicyForeign's contexts are ones the ledger never builds.

Smaller points: the concrete/*.sh scripts build their own contexts, some with malformed fields. The README wording "One input" for WalletRegister is inaccurate. The OwnAny scenarios use an ADA-pool datum only. isSuccessful counts any halted value, while V3 accepts only unit.

For each gap I give exact Lean for the owner to run. In every case the deployed bytes already reject the uncovered input in Aiken.

TxCert indices 0-10 (TxCert.lean:396-409), Delegatee, DRep, Voter, Vote, GovernanceActionId and ProposalProcedure match plutus-ledger-api V3 and stdlib v4's certificate.ak and governance.ak. RegisterCredential's deposit is an Option. MixLogicPurpose's isRegistration covers both cases, and Aiken halts on a registration with a Just deposit too.

The hand-written Data matches the Aiken types at the deployed commits: Proof Constr 0 [B z_b, B g_r_b, B vkh] and Register Constr 0 [B g, B u] (5b82530 schnorr.ak); the seedelf redeemer is B tag; the classic ReferenceDatum has 5 fields and v2's 8 fields, in order (types.ak at c1239fb and 5cc3631); MixDatum is Constr 0 [B a, B b]; Owner is Constr 0 [List [Constr 0 [B t, B z]]]; Mix is Constr 1 [List [Constr 0 [List [Constr 0 [B t0, B t1, B c, B z]]]]]; PayMixFee 0 / Replenish 1; the shard datum is unit.
The classic reference input in Logic.lean (f89cb43a…#0, 1,521,430 lovelace, the lovejoin NFT, denom 10 ₳, fee cap 1 ₳, the three hashes) matches c1239fb artifacts/mainnet/addresses.json.

Same-bytes cross-check: a Python mirror of the IsData instances (run/ledger.py) rebuilt every Steps.lean context and ran each with Aiken v1.1.24 on the same bytes: Seedelf 13/13, classic Lovejoin 17/17 (owner vector valid, other payout, z changed), v2 11/11 (KAT Mix and its variants, owner), templates 7/7. Every halt/error equals the trace's Steps line. Lean's v2 owner z passes on the mirror's bytes, so the two serialise outputs and refs identically.

Every Passes theorem's hypotheses (P≠"", bl≠0, tp≠"", tq≠0) exclude exactly the non-canonical Value encodings (a duplicate "" key, an explicit zero entry). So success directions are proved on canonical, ledger-shaped values.
Widening is harmless. Negative constructor indices (constrNeg), zero or negative amounts and duplicate keys appear only in families that also contain every reachable case (fails, or moves-for-all).

Template parameters are applied as Data constants (`toTerm P` = `(con data (B P))`), as `aiken blueprint apply` does. Aiken on the unapplied template hex with those arguments reproduces Template/Steps' verdicts (fee halts, a lovelace short errors, the 5 ₳ launch halts, minting two errors).
Recursor.map preserves list order (Recursors.lean:18-27), so inputs and outputs reach the script in the order written. Inputs in V2 Mix, OwnAny and OwnClassic are sorted by TxOutRef.

All five concrete/*.sh scripts, run today with TMPDIR in scratch, give their documented outcomes. lovejoin_owner.sh's context is string-equal to the mirror of Lean's ownerCtx, and its z equals Lean's.
The deployed wallet fails a non-Proof redeemer even with no datum (Aiken: I 0, a 2-field Constr and a wrong field type all error), so WalletNoLock's 'with any well-formed proof' wording is exact.
Owner withdrawals don't depend on the pool kind: the v2 owner vector halts with a token-pool ReferenceDatum and a token-holding box (validate_owner reads only M).

summary: Lane: the written claims against the proofs. I read SV/README.md, chunk-42 (status table, "What the claim can say" and every step), chunk-41's statuses and the doc comment of every Seedelf, Lovejoin, Template and V2 module. For each claim I found the theorems behind it. I checked the quoted counts, step counts, limits and hashes against the build traces and the extracted bytes, and ran the policy's own scenarios through Aiken's evaluator. Most of the record holds up. The counts match the traces (Lovejoin 276 = classic 46 + v2 230; Seedelf 28 traced + PolicyBurn's 2). Every quoted step count and script hash matches. Most module docs say what they fix, and the Owner and Mix families pair their failure theorems with a Lean-level passing theorem. But six things need fixing before this becomes the public "formally verified" claim. (1) PolicyAmount's and PolicyForeign's scenarios give the token the wrong name for their input, so every mint in them fails. Their ✅ test only the burn half of the README's "any amount other than ±1 fails" (Aiken agrees). (2) "What a ✅ is worth" leaves out established facts 3 to 5. The theorems are over NAME.prop, Blaster's optimized term, with nothing tying it to NAME.exec. isSuccessful is a halt with any value. An iff's failure side is only "no halt within the limit", and WalletRegister has no isUnsuccessful companion. The Steps runs that make the failure-only modules meaningful are unguarded #evals. (3) Several sentences claim more than their theorems: "every field symbolic", "any v2 pool", an unconditional "iff", "no value leaves the pool", "can't be replayed", "holds for any redeemer". (4) The README on this branch still describes the Seedelf-only build: no Lovejoin, PlutusCoreBlaster pinned at c7d8741 where the lakefile uses a local-only 68c5399, "three changes" where there are five, and SerializeData and XorByteString missing from the opaque list. (5) "What the claim can say" covers too much: the Seedelf policy, the classic pool's fee_contract and one_shot_mint, and a v2 that isn't on chain. (6) The launch conditions for v2's template theorems contradict each other. Also, this tree's record of the Seedelf ✅ predates the current pin. Short public sentences are possible. Seedelf: "Seedelf's wallet contract is formally verified on its deployed bytes: a Seedelf UTxO can be spent only with a valid Schnorr proof whose one-time key signs the transaction." Lovejoin v2: "Lovejoin v2's contracts are formally verified on their compiled bytes, for every pool launched from them: a mix of up to four boxes succeeds only if every box's one-of-n proof verifies and every box it pays goes back to the pool holding exactly the box value, and a withdrawal of up to four boxes succeeds only with each box's own proof, bound to the transaction." Each needs one caveat sentence: "The proofs are machine-checked by IOG's Blaster (Lean 4 and the Z3 solver) over IOG's model of the Plutus machine; they take the cryptography as given and cover one transaction shape per property." Four Lean check modules are in SCRATCH/claims/lean/Seedelf/, each with its expected output.
checked_ok: Theorem counts match the docs and the traces: step 1 = 30 (1+5+5+19), step 2 = 6, OwnClassic = 9, v2 = 230 (68 test-launch and template + 82 general Mix + 66 outputs + 14 OwnAny), Lovejoin = 276. Seedelf has 28 traced plus PolicyBurn's 2, the README's 30 (scratch traces.py).
Every Lovejoin and Seedelf trace on record has no error, no Undetermined, no unexpected Falsified and no sorry. The 321 blasterProven warnings are 276 + 28 + 17.

Every script hash the docs quote matches the extracted bytes (blake2b-224 over 0x03 ‖ script): 94bca9c0, 84967d91, 6777ba4d, c145c10f, 0dad3046, a072c7e8, f5592689, 288fea77, 7fb45b75, 2365a62d, 6878ed6f, 3698bbfd, 60294352. The Seedelf ones also match constants.rs:57-59.

WalletRegister's spec matches 5b82530's schnorr.prove and wallet.ak: scalar decode with 0 ≤ n < q, c = blake2b_224(g ‖ g_r ‖ u ‖ vkh), equal(scale(z, g), add(g_r, scale(c, u))), and list.has over the one signer.
PolicyBurn's #256 and -1 failure theorems are discriminating: the same scenario at #0 burns (Aiken: unit). The README row says exactly #256 or -1.
WalletNoLock's 18 shapes do cover every datum but Some(Constr 0 [B _, B _]), as the README says, by reading.
The README's 'defaultFunSemanticsVariantE' is right: Default/Basic.lean:54-55 makes it the default.
Rule 2's distinction holds in the model: cekExecuteProgram uses runStepsPreservingState, so exhaustion isn't Error. This comes from upstream 1c23de8 (#53), not from a fork change.
No axiom, sorry, admit, native_decide or implemented_by in Seedelf/ or Lovejoin/.

MixBoxGate and MixLogicPurpose pair each iff with an isUnsuccessful theorem. The Owner and Mix families pair failure theorems with a Lean-level Passes theorem. Each …Out builder is tied to its Mix by rfl (mixCtxOuts_is_the_mix).
MixChallenges' 'no lift' claim follows from the definitions: V2/MixSpec.lean:59-62's xor32 returns none for a non-32-byte operand, so the general Box theorems cover it.
The docs' limits on the classic pool (Mix unverified, withdrawals up to 3) and on v2 (Mix and withdrawals up to 4) match the modules.
chunk-41's upstream statuses are current (gh api): #71 is open at c60039c, #72 merged 2026-11-03, #73 is open at 5c048b0, #27 is open, and Lean-blaster #455 is open at 25c0ee0.
